sentences.text: In relation to the acquisition of four separate parcels of land owned by the petitioner, upon receiving notice under Section 15(2) of the Tamil Nadu Highways Act, 2001 (Tamil Nadu Highways Act), the 1st petitioner submitted objections on 24.04.2025.

entities.text: Tamil Nadu Highways Act, 2001 (Tamil Nadu Highways Act)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In those objections, the 1st petitioner pointed out that the proposed alignment divides the lands of the petitioner and other farmers and renders the remaining acquired lands unfit for purpose.
Therefore, the 1 st petitioner had proposed alternative alignments by even enclosing a sketch indicating such alternative alignments.
2. By referring to the communication dated 29.05.2025, learned counsel submits that it indicates that the objections of the 1st petitioner were not considered in any meaningful manner.
He submits that the objections were rejected by merely recording that the Highways Department experts decided on the alignment and the same cannot be changed.
Therefore, he contends that the matter warrants re-examination.
3. Learned Additional Advocate General responded to these submissions by pointing out that the order under Section 15(1) of the Highways Act was issued and that even the award is ready.
As regards the other petitioners before this Court, he submits that they executed conveyances in favour of the State.

Even as regards these petitioners, by referring to the statement given by the 1 st __________ Page3 of 8 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 06/02/2026 07:57:16 pm ) petitioner on 22.10.2025, he points out that he agreed that his land is not being divided as a result of the acquisition.
He also points out that the 1 st petitioner agreed to receive the compensation subject to objections and subject to the right to claim enhanced compensation under Section 64 of Act 30 of 2013.
In view of these developments, learned Additional Advocate General submitted that no case is made out to grant the relief claimed by the petitioners.
4. As submitted by learned counsel for the petitioners, the record shows that the 1st petitioner had submitted objections on 24.04.2025 suggesting alternative alignments.
It is also no doubt true that the proposal of the 1 st petitioner was not discussed while rejecting the request for change in alignments.
However, while the writ petition is pending, it appears that the 1 st petitioner has issued a statement on 22.10.2025.

In the said statement, the 1 st petitioner has stated as under:
__________ Page4 of 8 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
The 1st petitioner is the father of the second and third petitioners and has represented all the petitioners while raising objections and making the statement.
Thus, it appears that the petitioners have agreed to receive the compensation and even provided details of the bank account.
He has, however, made it clear that he is accepting the compensation subject to objections and subject to the right to seek enhanced compensation under Section 64 of Act 30 of 2013.

opennyai_summary.arguments: He also points out that the 1 st petitioner agreed to receive the compensation subject to objections and subject to the right to claim enhanced compensation under Section 64 of Act 30 of 2013.
opennyai_summary.decision:
